sections.h2: Foreign investors took out 57% of 2025-26's gross FDI inflow

chart.title: Repatriation took 64% of gross inflow in 2024-25, up from 25% in 2019-20
chart.sub: Repatriated money as a share of gross FDI inflow, %. Numbers beside each bar are US$ billion.

sections.means: Repatriation, not a fall in new investment, is now the main reason gross inflows fail to become net inflows.
sections.todo: Report net FDI next to the gross record in every headline figure, since the gross number alone overstates new foreign capital.

sections.h2: Net FDI fell from about $43 bn a year to $0.35 bn in 2024-25

chart.title: Net FDI fell to $0.35 bn in 2024-25, the lowest on record
chart.sub: Net FDI into India, US$ billion. 2024-25 is the first annual estimate and was later revised.

sections.means: Net FDI, the figure that helps pay for the current-account deficit, has shrunk to a small share of its pre-2022 level.
sections.todo: Treat the deficit financing gap as a planning risk, since portfolio flows and borrowing can reverse quickly.

sections.h2: Indian firms' investment abroad rose to $33 bn, 2.6 times the 2019-20 level

chart.title: Indian FDI abroad reached $33.3 bn in 2025-26, 2.6 times the 2019-20 level
chart.sub: Indian FDI abroad, US$ billion. 2023-24 uses the restated figure, with Indian FDI abroad as the residual.

sections.means: Outward investment by Indian companies now absorbs a large share of gross inflows and is a second reason net FDI is low.
sections.todo: Track outward FDI alongside inward FDI so that the balance-of-payments effect of both is visible.
